task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently at home in the United States.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
I've pulled up your account, John. Let me check a few things on the network side first.

Account check for line **555-123-2002** (line ID L1002):
- Line status: **Active** (not suspended)
- Plan: **Premium Plan**, 15 GB monthly data
- Current usage: **8.7 GB used of 15 GB** (cycle ends 2025-02-28) — so you haven't hit your data limit
- No overdue bills on the account that would restrict service

So the account and line look healthy. That means the issue is most likely on the device or its network settings. To narrow it down, could you tell me:

1. What do you see at the **top of your screen** (status bar) right now — do you see signal bars and a network type like 5G, LTE/4G, 3G, or do you see "No Signal"?
2. Are you currently **inside your normal home coverage area**, or are you traveling outside it?
3. Does the problem happen **everywhere**, or only in certain locations?
4. Are you connected to **Wi-Fi** at the moment?

Good news — that airplane symbol is actually a very simple fix, nothing is broken with your account or your line. 😊

**What it means:** Airplane Mode is switched ON on your phone. That's a setting that deliberately turns off all of the phone's wireless connections — cellular service, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth — which is why you have no signal bars at all and no internet. It's easy to switch on by accident, so please don't worry; it's not something you did wrong and it isn't "bad."

Here's how to turn it off:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen** (swipe down again if needed) to open the quick settings panel.
2. Look for the **airplane / ✈️ icon** — it's currently highlighted/colored in.
3. **Tap it once** so it turns grey or turns off.
4. Wait about **10–20 seconds** and then look at the top of your screen again.

After that, you should see signal bars reappear along with a network type (like 5G, LTE, or 4G) near the battery icon.

Could you try that now and tell me **exactly what you see at the top of your screen afterward** — the signal bars and any letters like 5G, LTE/4G, 3G or E?

Once I know that, I can check whether your mobile data is also switched on and whether there's anything else slowing it down.
turns.execution_output: User: All right, I'll try that. Let me find that airplane icon...

turns.thought:
Good progress — the airplane mode is off and you now have a signal! You're right that 2G is old, and there are two separate things to fix here. Let's take them one at a time.

**First, the most important one: your mobile data is switched off.** That's why the internet isn't working at all. (2G is slow, but with data off you get nothing.)

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data ON:**
1. Swipe down from the very top of your screen **twice** so you see a full panel of round/square buttons (the quick settings).
2. Look for the button with the words **"Mobile data"** — it may also look like two little up/down arrows, and it's probably greyed out or crossed off right now.
3. **Tap it** so it lights up / turns on.
4. Wait about 10–20 seconds.

*(If you don't see it there, no problem — instead open **Settings** → **Connections** (or **Network & Internet**) → **Mobile network** → and switch **Mobile data** to ON.)*

Once that's done, try opening a webpage or your email, and tell me what happens.

I'll walk you through the 2G part right after that — but let's do this one first, since it's the one stopping your internet entirely. Let me know when you've tapped it!
turns.execution_output: User: All right, let me try to find that mobile data button...

turns.thought:
Excellent — "Data Enabled" is exactly what we wanted! 🎉 Now let's deal with the other two things you spotted. You have a good eye.

**The downward arrow = Data Saver mode.** Yes, I'm afraid that one *does* slow things down. It's a battery/data-saving feature that restricts how apps use data in the background, which makes the internet feel sluggish and makes some apps seem stuck. Let's turn it off.

**Step 2 — Turn Data Saver OFF (via Settings):**
1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Connections** (on some phones it's **Network & Internet**)
3. Tap **Data usage**
4. Tap **Data Saver** (you may also see it called "Data Saver mode")
5. Switch it **OFF / Disable**

*(Some phones also let you turn it off right from the quick settings panel: swipe down from the top of your screen twice and look for the **"Data Saver"** tile — tap it so it's no longer highlighted.)*

**Step 3 — Change off 2G**

You're right that 2G is old — it's the oldest, slowest network type, which is why your signal reads "Poor" and speeds crawl. Let's tell the phone to prefer the fast modern networks instead:

1. Open **Settings**
2. Tap **Connections** (or **Network & Internet**)
3. Tap **Mobile networks**
4. Tap **Network mode** (sometimes called "Preferred network mode")
5. Select **5G/4G/3G auto** or **"5G/LTE preferred"** — *anything except 2G*

**Step 4 — Restart your phone**

After changing network settings, it's important to restart so the changes fully take effect:
- Hold the **power button**, then tap **Restart / Reboot**
- Wait for it to come back on (~30–60 seconds)

When it's back on, check the top of your screen again and try loading a webpage or your email.

**Please tell me what you now see:** the signal strength (Poor/Fair/Good/Excellent), the network type (5G / LTE / 4G / 3G / 2G), and whether the downward arrow is gone. And let me know if the internet works properly now — or still doesn't. We'll keep going either way.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh my, that's a lot of steps all at once. I'm afraid I can only do one thing at a time — my head gets all muddled otherwise. Could you tell me just the first one to do?

And... about restarting the phone — will that delete my photos? I have pictures of my grandchildren on there and I'd be ever so upset if I lost them.

turns.thought:
Of course — one thing at a time, I completely understand. And first, let me put your mind at ease:

**No, a restart will NOT delete your photos.** A restart (also called a reboot or power cycle) simply turns your phone off and back on again. Your photos, videos, contacts, messages and apps are all stored safely inside the phone's memory, and they stay exactly where they are. It's no different from turning off a television and turning it back on. Also, those photos of your grandchildren are almost certainly saved to your phone's storage permanently, so nothing can remove them by restarting. Please don't worry about that one bit.

Now, **just the first thing to do.** One step only:

👉 **Please turn OFF Data Saver** — that's the little downward arrow symbol you can see.

The quickest way is usually straight from the screen you're already on:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen, then swipe down again**, so you get the full panel of those little square buttons.
2. Look for the one that says **"Data Saver"** — it may have the downward arrow on it, and it's currently lit up/colored in.
3. **Tap it once** so it turns grey / is no longer highlighted.

Can you see a "Data Saver" button in that panel? If it's not there, tell me and I'll give you the other way to find it using your Settings menu.

Just do that one thing, then let me know — and I'll give you the next single step.

turns.thought:

Next single thing. It's a small one — please **restart your phone**:

2. When a menu appears on screen, tap **"Restart"** (if you see "Power off" instead, tap that, wait for the screen to go completely black, then press and hold the power button again to switch it back on).
3. Wait about **30–60 seconds** for it to come back to life.

Remember — this won't touch your photos. Everything stays exactly as it is.

The reason we're doing this now is so that your phone goes and reconnects to the network fresh, with the Data Saver change properly applied.

Once it's back on, **look at the top of your screen and tell me what it says** — the signal strength (Poor/Fair/Good/Excellent), the network type (2G / 3G / 4G / LTE / 5G), and whether it still says "Data Enabled."

That's it — just that one thing now. I'll give you the next single step after you're back.

Once you tap it, it'll usually save automatically and take you back a screen.

That's the only thing to do now. After you've picked it, **tell me what option you selected** (or if you couldn't find it, tell me what you did see on that screen) — and then I'll give you the next single step.

We're getting close — 2G is very likely the last piece of the puzzle.
